dialogue.content: こんにちは。相談員です。
dialogue.English: Hello. I'm the counselor.

dialogue.content: こんにちは。よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Hello. Thank you for seeing me.

dialogue.content: はじめに性別、年齢、お住いの都道府県を教えてください。
dialogue.English: To begin, could you please tell me your gender, age, and the prefecture where you live?

dialogue.content: 42歳　女性　東京都在住です。
dialogue.English: I'm a 42-year-old woman living in Tokyo.

dialogue.content: 教えていただきありがとうございます。今日は、どんなご相談でいらっしゃいましたか。
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. What brings you here today?

dialogue.content: 父との関係に悩んでいます。去年の夏、両親が北海道旅行で車の正面衝突事故に遭い、母が瀕死の状態で2ヶ月間の入院と積極的治療で回復をしました。
dialogue.English: I'm struggling with my relationship with my father. Last summer, my parents were in a head-on car collision while traveling in Hokkaido. My mother was near death and recovered after two months of hospitalization and intensive treatment.

dialogue.content: 事故にあったというよりは、その事故を起こしたのは父の居眠り運転でした。
dialogue.English: It wasn't just that they were in an accident; it was caused by my father falling asleep at the wheel.

dialogue.content: 当初は、回復も難しく死んでしまう可能性が90％以上と言われて、私も姉二人も悲しみに暮れる毎日でした。愛する母をそんな目に遭わせた父に対する憎しみがあります
dialogue.English: At first, we were told her chances of recovery were slim, with over a 90% chance she could die. My two older sisters and I were grief-stricken every day. I feel hatred toward my father for putting my beloved mother through that.

dialogue.content: 母が昏睡状態の時に、もう運転は2度としないでほしいと言いましたが、母が回復し関東に戻れた時には、「自分の余生もある。反省してる。注意をしながらまた運転はするつもり、」と言われてそんな発言をする父が許せず、疎遠になりました。
dialogue.English: While my mother was in a coma, I told him I wanted him to never drive again. But when she recovered and was able to return to the Kanto area, he said, 'I still have the rest of my life. I regret what happened. I intend to drive again, being careful.' I couldn't forgive him for saying that, and we became estranged.

dialogue.content: 母や姉は　父も反省しているし、、、と言って私とは真逆の意見です。孫や他の家族のために、修復をした方がいいのか悩んでいます。
dialogue.English: My mother and sisters say that he is remorseful... and they take the opposite view from me. I'm torn about whether I should try to repair the relationship for the sake of the grandchildren and the rest of the family.

dialogue.content: ご両親が旅行中に大きな事故にあわれたのですね。お母さまを危険な目に合わせ、辛い思いをされたお父様との関係を修復した方がいいか悩んでいるのですね。
dialogue.English: So your parents were in a major accident during their trip, weren't they? And you're struggling with whether to repair your relationship with your father, who put your mother in danger and caused you so much pain.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。。
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right...

dialogue.content: 何とお呼びしたら良いでしょうか
dialogue.English: What would you like me to call you?

dialogue.content: みゆきでお願いします。
dialogue.English: Please call me Miyuki.

dialogue.content: みゆきさん。大切なお母さまをそのような危ない状態に、それも居眠り運転をしていたお父様に対して憎しみの感情を抱くのは自然のことと思います。
dialogue.English: Miyuki, I think it's natural to feel hatred toward your father, given that his falling asleep at the wheel put your beloved mother in such a dangerous state.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: お母さまとは連絡を取っているのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Are you in contact with your mother?

dialogue.content: 本当は色々辛かった時期が思い出されて母含め姉達とも関わりをやめたかったのですが、
dialogue.English: To be honest, remembering those very painful times made me want to cut off contact with my mother and my sisters as well, but...

dialogue.content: 母が私の子ども達を生まれてからずっとかわいがり、いつも今でも気にしてくれて
dialogue.English: my mother has doted on my children since they were born and still always cares about them,

dialogue.content: そこを切ってしまうのは可哀想だなと思い、母とは取っています。
dialogue.English: I felt it would be a pity to cut that connection, so I've stayed in touch with my mother.

dialogue.content: リハビリがすすみ、本人も頑張った今事故前の60%まで体力が戻り、今は千葉から都内までまた孫を見に来ることを目標にしています。
dialogue.English: Her rehabilitation is progressing, and thanks to her hard work, she has regained 60% of her pre-accident physical strength. Her goal now is to be able to come from Chiba to Tokyo to see her grandchildren again.

dialogue.content: 優しいお母さまなのですね。今でもお孫さんの顔を見るためにつらいリハビリを頑張ってらっしゃるのですね。
dialogue.English: She sounds like a very kind mother. She's enduring difficult rehabilitation just so she can see her grandchildren's faces again.

dialogue.content: そうなんです。慈愛に満ちた母で、誰にでも優しく温かい母です
dialogue.English: Yes, she is. She is full of compassion—kind and warm to everyone.

dialogue.content: 健康に70まで来て、それがあの事故で今まで100%で楽しんでいた事が出来なくなってしまった
dialogue.English: She had been healthy up to age 70, and that accident took away her ability to enjoy things as fully as she used to.

dialogue.content: みゆきさんがお母さまを大切に思う理由がよくわかりました。
dialogue.English: I can clearly understand why you cherish your mother so much, Miyuki.

dialogue.content: その状況を作った父に腹が立ちます
dialogue.English: I'm furious with my father for creating this situation.

dialogue.content: そう思いますよね。
dialogue.English: It makes sense that you would feel that way.

dialogue.content: 父は考え方が全く違い日本語を話していても話が通じない感じがします
dialogue.English: My father thinks so differently; it feels like even when we're speaking Japanese, we can't communicate.

dialogue.content: 結局話が平行線で、疎遠になりました。
dialogue.English: In the end, our conversations went nowhere, and we became estranged.

dialogue.content: どんなお父様なのですか。具体的に、どんなところが苦手なのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: What is your father like? Specifically, what do you find difficult about him?

dialogue.content: 父は、23歳から外地でずっと色々な仕事を成し遂げ、高い登山にも挑戦したり、65で引退してからは母と旅行や登山、海を楽しんでいました。上記のことからかなり自分に対する過信があり、73になって体力や判断力の低下を周りが感じ伝えても聞き入れませんでした
dialogue.English: From the age of 23, my father accomplished many things working abroad, challenged himself with high-altitude mountaineering, and after retiring at 65, he enjoyed traveling, hiking, and the sea with my mother. Because of all this, he is overly confident in himself, and at 73, he wouldn't listen even when those around him noticed and told him his physical strength and judgment were declining.

dialogue.content: いつか、運転やめてと言おうと思っていた矢先の事故でした。
dialogue.English: The accident happened just as I was thinking that I needed to tell him to stop driving.

dialogue.content: そういう意味では、私は、父に強く言えない母にも腹が立っていたんだと思います。
dialogue.English: In that sense, I think I was also angry at my mother for not being able to be firm with my father.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね。いつごろから、お父様に苦手な感情が湧くようになったのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: I see. Around when did you start to have these difficult feelings toward your father?

dialogue.content: そう言われてみると...小学生の頃からだったかもしれません。
dialogue.English: Now that you mention it... it may have been since I was in elementary school.

dialogue.content: 小学校の頃、なにかきっかけがあったのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Was there any particular trigger when you were in elementary school?

dialogue.content: 厳格で小6だった姉が父の友人に敬語を使わずビンタをしたり、いつも機嫌が悪く、末娘の私は怖いが故、いつも父の機嫌を取ることを考えていました
dialogue.English: He was strict; when my sister was in the sixth grade, he slapped her for not using polite language with one of his friends. He was always in a bad mood, and as the youngest daughter, I was so afraid that I was always thinking about how to keep him appeased.

dialogue.content: それは怖い思いをされましたね。いつもお父様を怒らせないようにと気をつかっていたのですね。
dialogue.English: That must have been very scary for you. You were always careful not to make your father angry.

dialogue.content: お父様の優しい時はありましたか。
dialogue.English: Were there times when your father was kind?

dialogue.content: そうなんです。尊敬しているようでいつも逃げたくて仕方なかったかもしれません。
dialogue.English: Yes. It might have seemed like I respected him, but I always desperately wanted to get away.

dialogue.content: やさしいときは、皆を旅行に連れて行ってくれたりした時ですかね。
dialogue.English: The kind times... I guess it was when he would take us all on trips.

dialogue.content: そう言われて振り返ってみると、今根底の自分の正直な父に対する気持ちが、昔からだったかもしれないと思いました。
dialogue.English: Now that you say that and I look back, I realize that my underlying, honest feelings toward my father may have been there since long ago.

dialogue.content: そのみゆきさんのお気持ちをきいてくてくれる人はいますか。
dialogue.English: Is there anyone you can talk to about these feelings?

dialogue.content: 友人が一人、唯一知っていますのでその人ですかね。
dialogue.English: I have one friend—the only person who knows—so I suppose it would be her.

dialogue.content: みゆきさんの気持ちを聴いてくれる、ご友人がいらっしゃるのですね。
dialogue.English: So you have a friend who listens to your feelings.

dialogue.content: はい、そう言った意味では必要な時に相談に乗ってくれるので楽かもしれません
dialogue.English: Yes, in that sense, it might be a relief because she's there for me to talk to when I need her.

dialogue.content: みゆきさんのお父様に対する感情は当然だと思います。一人で抱え込まずに思いを聞いてもらってください
dialogue.English: Miyuki, I think your feelings toward your father are completely natural. Please don't keep them bottled up; let someone listen to you.

dialogue.content: はい。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Yes. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: こちらにもまたご連絡ください。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: Please feel free to contact us again. Thank you.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.
